title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
abstract: arXiv:2611.07667v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The performance of multi-agent LLM systems depends not only on the capabilities of the underlying models but also on information-sharing policies, which govern what information each agent observes and at what level of detail. But does providing AI agents with more detailed information always improve collective outcomes, or can transparency paradoxically degrade efficiency? To investigate this, we introduce empirical information design, an experimental framework that systematically compares disclosure policies across economic markets populated by LLM agents, while holding interaction rules and models fixed. We evaluate ten frontier LLMs in multi-resource trade, bilateral bargaining, and double auctions, using ground-truth utilities to decouple identified opportunities from realized outcomes. We find that finer information disclosure yields highly model-dependent results. In trade, revealing exact valuations rather than ordinal preference

translated_title: 谁应该知道什么？面向多智能体LLM经济的实证信息设计
translated_abstract: 多智能体LLM系统的性能不仅取决于底层模型的能力，还取决于信息共享策略，即决定每个智能体观察到什么信息以及以何种详细程度的规则。但是，为AI智能体提供更详细的信息是否总能改善集体结果？或者透明度是否会悖论地降低效率？为了研究这个问题，我们提出了实证信息设计，这是一个实验框架，在保持交互规则和模型固定不变的情况下，系统地比较由LLM智能体组成的经济市场中不同的信息披露策略。我们在多资源交易、双边议价和双向拍卖场景中评估了十个前沿LLM，并使用真实效用数据将已识别的机会与已实现的结果解耦。我们发现，更精细的信息披露会产生高度依赖于模型的结果。在交易中，揭示精确估值而非序数偏好
tldr: 该论文提出“实证信息设计”实验框架，通过在由LLM智能体构成的经济市场中系统比较不同的信息披露策略，发现更详细的信息透明度并不总能改善集体结果，其效果高度依赖于具体模型。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an empirical information design framework that systematically compares disclosure policies across economic markets populated by LLM agents, finding that finer information transparency does not always improve collective outcomes, with effects highly dependent on the specific model.
